newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Madonna is not that sexy, says Argentine president.
newsitem.headline: Madonna is not that sexy, says Argentine president.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem, stung by Madonna's comments about him and his country, said on Tuesday he did not find the pop star attractive when they met.
"Madonna is not such a big deal. I didn't feel fascinated or attracted by her," the Peronist leader told reporters.
In her diary of the making of the movie "Evita," the steamy pop star described her secret rendezvous with the 67-year-old president on an island near Buenos Aires in February.
Madonna, who had her first baby on Monday, said her conversation with Menem delved into "mysticism and reincarnation" and "we were both mutually impressed."
She said Menem stared at her bra-strap and "didn't take his eyes off me," her diary published in Vanity Fair magazine said.
Madonna wanted to overcome Menem's reservations about her movie portrayal of Eva Peron, the legendary wife of populist leader Juan Domingo Peron who was loved by Argentina's poor.
She managed to persuade Menem to let her sing "Don't Cry For Me Argentina" on the famous balcony of the Casa Rosada presidential palace from where Peron addressed mass meetings.

Madonna, who was greeted by graffiti saying "Viva Evita! Madonna Out!," called Argentina an "uncivilized country...with no gymnasiums or decent food. The only way to eat sensibly in this country is not to eat" -- harsh words for a country proud of producing the best beef in the world.
Menem, a divorcee whose fondness for Argentine women even spills over into his political speeches, said his country has "thousands or millions of women more attractive and prettier than Madonna."
"Argentina has women of amazing beauty. When you are out walking you see them and you really don't know which way to turn," said the president.
"Evita," based on the hit British musical of the 1970s and directed by Alan Parker, is due for release in December.
